analysis: All three changed files are test-only: a new EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift, a doc-comment change in SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift, and a fixture change in GPTOSSCheckpointRestartFixture.swift. They add no production code, no network or auth surface and no key handling. No changed line touches the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, fan helper or cache crypto. The tests exercise EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry and productionSchedulerConfig, whose implementation is not in the supplied batch. They assert a wider 2048-token plain chunk for GPT-OSS, Gemma 4 text and dense Qwen, and that paged-pool ring sizing is unchanged (max(chunk, stripe)). They also assert bidirectional media stays at the SDK chunk, and that malformed environment overrides fall back to the SDK geometry. This touches availability and memory-footprint concerns such as T-010 and T-029 and the paged-pool sizing for TB-007. The production change is not visible here, so any effect on pool sizing or admission limits needs review in the corresponding source diff. The tests only assert that the invariant holds. The fixture's new `environment` override merges into the production-build environment in test code only. It defaults to empty, and `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` is still set when store is nil. The fixture creates a test-owned temp root and an ephemeral key, so the SSD cache (T-041) posture is unchanged. The step-budget and chunk environment keys are operator-controlled local configuration. The tests show that Int.max saturates without overflow and that nonpositive values fall back. The remaining question is whether the production geometry code, not in this batch, enforces those fallbacks and how a huge operator-set chunk interacts with ring sizing.
